Lions in Laos

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
Treatment/ Planning Lions in Lao
This is a story about how lions are being used to supply bones to the tiger market in Asia for millions of rands. We have our heroes this side like Smaragda Louw from BAT who has been trying to make the South African law makers aware of this, and knows about the people who participate in this unethical market. Then there is Karl Amman, a film maker who has spent his life trying to expose harm that has come to animals like rhino horn trade, elephant tusk trade and tiger bone wine trade. They are the characters in this story that will speak to the audience on an emotional scale.
Because this is about lions and tigers, I will ask my contacts at Lorypark zoo if I can film their lions and tigers, close up, really get intimate shots – we can do links as well there.
Karl Amman is coming on the 26th – catching a connecting flight at OR Tambo back to Kenya from Europe. It wont be enough time for an interview, but he wants to sit down with me and help with footage etc. He has said he will sign the footage release for his footage from his doccie tiger bone wine trade – and he has sent that voice message about just covering the costs of the stringers on the ground who captured the footage in Laos. He explained it well in the message, and I think this clarifies everything and is something you’ll hopefully be happy with.
In terms of capturing these animals – I need to go to 4PAWS who are in Bethlehem, they know the farm where these animals originated from, and will be able to speak about the history of this issue in South Africa: the issue in broadstrokes: We have captive bred lions around the country who just were bred and bred, and then Covid hit and none of them could be hunted. They were already exporting lion bones – to substitute for tiger bones… for the “Tiger bone/tiger wine” market – this was because people in Vietnam use it like Rhino horn- either grinding it into a powder or drinking the “wine” they make. So obviously there aren’t enough tigers in the world, so then “substituting” lions for the tiger bone trade – in which is the only real difference is SIZE. And so the end user in Asia often isn’t even getting the actual tiger bone wine, but lion bone. Our story will that even further…
According to the permits: Farm Energie (Robbie Prinsloo) in Bethlehem has sold lionesses (2 of which were pregnant) the name on the permits is Mary Goldbaltt (who used to be Prinsloo) is now the CHIEF EXECUTIVE OF THE SOUTH AFRICAN PREDATORS ASSOCIATION – SAPA.
Then we have African Pride Import & Exports (Edward Coetzer in Boksburg) on the permit which are the guys who get the permits and supposedly travel with the animals. Edward Coetzer’s business partner Philip Fourie has been given a criminal record for smuggling animals – but for some strange reason, South African laws allow someone to continue in the same trade after a conviction?! This is something Smargada can speak to the history of the import/exporters and their conduct.
She will also speak to the fact that CITES and South African government are saying they want to close down the supply of lion bones to Asia, but they are doing it really slowly – like with this new legislation that adds in the “welfare” aspect of these animals.
Then we get on the ground in Laos and that’s where we will have Karl and the footage there. Essentially he has had it transcribed and has given us the details of the place there – but these animals were sent to a “zoo” that isn’t even built yet. Also no one can afford zoos there, he will explain why Laos and how it works, and this is clearly and attempt to set up a breeding facility to then continue sending lions bones into the tiger bone trade because if South Africa is getting a little bit more difficult, those selling it know there will come a time when its ended. There are practically no animal welfare laws in Laos, and it’s a hub to country’s that surround it.

Summary:
Filming schedule:
DAY 1:
1. I would need a presenter to interview Smaragda – but we need time to actually be with her and her animals and see why she became this advocate for animals – she’s the type of crazy that goes and stands at zoo/circus corners holding banners and shouting at the owners to let the animals go. Her goal in life is the ban the trade in animals (BAT). AND I don’t think we’ve ever really highlighted this part of her, we have shown it in short snippets but we haven’t really told her story and who she is. She’s very passionate and I think quite a character that an audience can empathize with – you don’t have to be an animal lover to understand her.
2. I would then go to Boksburg and film outside African Pride, and we should go knock on their door to ask for an interview with a presenter. I think we need to see the faces of the people involved – so the audience can understand.
3. We would go to midrand and film the lions and tigers up close and personal – do some presenter links.

DAY 2/3:
1. We need the presenter to come with us to Bethlehem and interview 4PAWS, we will then speak about the breeder of these lions and try to understand why they sold them/ their history etc – we will then call them and try to go to the farm – I’m not expecting to gain access there, but I do think we should be able to gain answers – they are one of many exporters of wild animals and I think we need to highlight the trade and the cruelty that comes with it. If we don’t get them, my plan is to still incorporate them with the presenter – we will do some snooping shots – showing the presenter researching them, trying to go see them, and this will add the dimension of secrecy that surrounds this trade – no one wants to be known as a lion exporter – its not something one fesses up to.
I think we will need some time to also travel which take 3-4 hours – so travel time would be ideal.
2. We also still need to interview Karl Amman – and he said he will film himself and get footage of him from his doccies and things – so that is quite sorted – we can create his character as this person who wants to expose the trade and he has been able to have some impact in Asia with his documentary’s. It’s a very tough place to make a dent, so we can explain that. I’m not sure if we will have time enough with a presenter to do this, and I’m not sure Zoom can really help with the personal feel I have so I may just do the interview myself. Karl is german, his family are from kenya/Seychelles and he basically grew up in “wild” Africa and has been saddened and disheartened to see our animals used for pets/body parts etc So he can explain this as well really nicely – we can even include some of his childhood – giving him also a dimension in the piece.



Further information:
We also need to put questions to CITES and the ministry – Barbara Creecy intv request. But I don’t expect either to agree, as they haven’t in the past. So with regards to their right of reply’s and the farm in Laos, I suggest we potentially have the presenter read them? Or Someone else voicing them? We need to come up with a different device for them, so the responses aren’t just washed away – but also aren’t boring.

Script:


LIONS TO LAOS
South Africa …
one of the world’s top wildlife destinations, but one that’s long grappled with the dark side of its lion tourism: Canned trophy hunting, cub petting…and lion bone harvesting for the Asian traditional medicine market - dubious practices that have fueled the expansion of lion farms for decades.
Farms where possibly ten thousand lions have been bred - in captivity - to meet an insatiable demand.
UPSOUND NATSOUND
It’s caused Brand SA’s conservation reputation to take a hit.
From his remote home in Kenya, wildlife activist Karl Ammann (ah-mun) investigates wildlife trafficking.
Karl: South African image is at stake here to some extent because if the tourists know what's going on behind the closed doors of this breeding and this butchering of lions they don't like to hear or be told that aspect.
But Karl's biggest investigation was into the illicit trade in South-East Asia of another apex predator - tigers…
Hunted to near-extinction, and now also farmed in captivity for their body parts used in traditional medicine… and bones, mixed in wine for a sought-after status symbol.
Karl: So you go into a restaurant and there's a big fish tank with a tiger skeleton in the fish tank. And then there's a little faucet on the side and you can feel your glass there and half and after dinner drink of tiger wine.
In 2015 Amman’s documentary on the so-called 'Tiger Bone Mafia' revealed how tiger populations had declined…the trade was banned …and the tiger mafia set their sights on South Africa… where lion bones were readily available.
In other words, Lion bones would now be sold as Tiger bones.
PAUSE / music
Discarded when hunting trophies are mounted, they’re easy to pass off as tiger bones - and for some time, the South African government has allowed their export.
PAUSE / music
But animal activists were fighting back.
By 2019 South Africa’s Constitutional Court banned lion bone trading… and two years later Environment Minister Barbara Creecy said the government intended to shut down the captive lion industry altogether.
Creecy: ‘They will not be hunting animals that have been taken out of the cage and put in their pathway.’
But would the tiger mafia take this lying down?
The story of a fake zoo that emerged in Laos this year suggests they haven’t.
DIP TO BLACK TRANSITION
In September this year, Amman discovered the tiger mafia’s next move, when ten live lions - among them pregnant lionesses - were exported from South Africa to Laos - a tiger farming hotspot.
Pause
Karl believed the export was an effort to establish a new lion breeding facility in Laos to generate a supply of bones.
The welfare organisation Four Paws says the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species or CITES allowed the export under a zoo permit.
Kieran: Laos has said that the lions went for a zoo, that's another fear from our side that what used to be a blatant commercial trade is being disguised as a zoo trade, and we just hope that it isn't gonna turn into a lion farm on the other side.
IF their destination wasn’t a zoo, the deal would be illegal.
We enlisted an undercover agent who works with Amman, to investigate on the ground in Laos.
Karl: Obviously to them it all just look like the tiger farms the same the same structure the same pattern of caging and so on.
The agent filmed the lions shortly after their arrival. The lionesses had given birth.
Karl: Some females were shipped in a pregnant stage which shouldn't have been happening, certainly not in the last trimester of pregnancy.
After the trauma of travel, one lost all five cubs. The lioness with two surviving cubs was separated from her offspring. The investigator was told what their future would hold.
Karl: They met some of the players but yeah they will get more lions, and they will breed these lions, they will sell live lions, cubs as pets and they will do the lion bone trade.
The property looked nothing like a zoo: no outdoor signage, display cages or educational programmes. The only other animals were a lonely monkey … and some tigers. His experience told Amman it looked just like a captive breeding facility.
But who signed the paperwork for such a deal? Who made it legal at a time when lion farms are facing closure?
Transition to next act
We took the CITES permits that an anonymous source leaked to us to the founder of Ban Animal Trading, Smaragda Louw.
UPS SMARAGDA (GRAPHIC)
Smaragda could see that the ten lions had been sold by a Free State lion farmer called Robbie Prinsloo of Farm Energie, and Edward Coetzer of African Pride Import and Export who shipped the Lions via Malaysia to Laos.
Smaragda: The permit was in the name of Robbie Prinsloo. Edward Coetzer of African Pride was then the agent, he exported the animals to this so-called zoo in Laos.
Smaragda had encountered Prinsloo’s Lions before in the course of her work.
Smaragda: There's a lot of trade happening amongst all the people who breed lions. We know animals from the Rhino and Lion Park in Krugersdorp were sold to Farm Energy.
It’s a reputational hazard for South Africa, fighting to restore its image as an ethical wildlife destination – YET a captive-bred lion that a tourist sees today… may end up in the hands of the tiger bone mafia tomorrow.
We set out to find Farm Energie…
Mac gets out car, goes to sign, checks out place…
Prinsloo wouldn’t let us onto his farm, but said he loved his lions.
Phone call: Mac: Robbie you’re speaking to MacFarlane from Carte Blanche.
Prinsloo: Ja?
Mac: I want to know about lions that went to Laos?
Prinsloo: All the paperwork, as well as the legit paperwork from Laos government were for a zoo. I was actually proud to do this whole deal with them, because my lions will be going to a zoo, and millions of hundreds of people will be able to see them.
Mac: All I can say is that you might have made a big big mistake, and sent your animals to the slaughter?
Prinsloo: Ya, that’s… I don’t want to hear it, because I really love my lions.
Through his lawyer, Prinsloo denied any involvement in the transaction. But he dropped names of two people involved in the deal, who are NOT on the CITES permits…
Prinsloo: I can give you the woman who was helping me with all the paperwork, is Maryn. You know there were a guy from Joburg, that did this whole export thing, Gideon Fourie.
Maryn is Maryn Goldblatt the former Head of the South African Predator Association which should be overseeing the big cat industry, including the animals’ welfare. It seems she didn’t know where the lions would end up either.
Maryn: Yes, I just helped him with the permits, and everything with the agents, that’s all I did.
Mac: The issue here, is where the animals are going to end up?
Maryn: Any lion that we sell can end up either in a hunt, or killed or anything. They gave us their assurance that the animals are going to be in a good facility. So, I don’t know really what your problem is.
Prinsloo told us that Gideon Fourie was the exporter, but he’s nowhere on the permits, and that might be with good reason: Ban Animal Trading encountered Fourie when he was convicted in 2017 of trafficking cockatoos, parrots, and monkeys and was given a suspended prison sentence and R85,000 fine.
Smaragda intv: That export alone was worth R645,000, his companies kept exporting animals, and he continues as usual
We tried to ask Fourie about this transaction…
Call with Fourie: Fourie: Hello? Mac: Hi, it’s MacFarlane from Carte Blanche.
BOOP BOOP BOOP (hangs up)
In later texts, Fourie said he wanted nothing to do with our story.
(graphic)
Our final request for clarity… the exporter, Edward Coetzer of African Pride Import and Export who declined to speak, but sent documents showing it was the State Vet’s decision to allow lionesses to travel pregnant.
Coetzer sent us these videos of the lions in Laos as proof of their “well-being”.
UPS: VIDEO
Barbara Creecy’s Department didn’t respond on why heavily pregnant lionesses were allowed to travel.
CITES hasn't told us why the facility was given a zoo classification.
Kieran: Laos announced that they would close their tiger farms, they have yet to do that.
With no online presence, it proved impossible to speak to the Laos facility managers.
In the meantime, South Africa’s lions continue to pay a high price. 11.05
END



Promo 1 - 21 seconds

A shipment of ten lions is sent from South Africa to an East Asian country well known for its illicit trade in wildlife body parts.
UPSOUND: Karl: So you go into a restaurant and there's a big fish tank with a tiger skeleton in the fish tank. And then there's a little faucet on the side and you can filll your glass there and half and after dinner drink of tiger wine.
We investigate what happened to these lions - and uncover that all is not as it seems.

Promo two - 21 seconds

It was a shipment of ten healthy lions from South Africa to an East Asian country, that caused animal activists to raise the alarm.
Upsound : Kieran: we just hope that it isn't gonna turn into a lion farm on the other side.
VO: Sent to a country well known for the illicit trade of animal parts - we investigate what really happened to these apex predators.


Promo 3 - 21 seconds

Lion farming… tiger bones and the illicit trade of wild animals and their body parts….
Upsound: Kieran: Laos announced that they would close their tiger farms, they have yet to do that.
VO: We investigate how ten healthy lions shipped from South Africa, were allegedly condemned to die in East Asia

In 2015 Amman’s documentary on the so-called 'Tiger Bone Mafia' revealed how tiger populations had declined…the trade was banned …and the tiger mafia set their sights on South Africa… where lion bones were readily available. In other words, Lion bones would now be sold as Tiger bones. PAUSE / music Discarded when hunting trophies are mounted, they’re easy to pass off as tiger bones - and for some time, the South African government has allowed their export. PAUSE / music But animal activists were fighting back. By 2019 South Africa’s Constitutional Court banned lion bone trading… and two years later Environment Minister Barbara Creecy said the government intended to shut down the captive lion industry altogether. Creecy: ‘They will not be hunting animals that have been taken out of the cage and put in their pathway.’ But would the tiger mafia take this lying down? The story of a fake zoo that emerged in Laos this year suggests they haven’t. DIP TO BLACK TRANSITION In September this year, Amman discovered the tiger mafia’s next move, when ten live lions - among them pregnant lionesses - were exported from South Africa to Laos - a tiger farming hotspot. Pause Karl believed the export was an effort to establish a new lion breeding facility in Laos to generate a supply of bones. The welfare organisation Four Paws says the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species or CITES allowed the export under a zoo permit. Kieran: Laos has said that the lions went for a zoo, that's another fear from our side that what used to be a blatant commercial trade is being disguised as a zoo trade, and we just hope that it isn't gonna turn into a lion farm on the other side. IF their destination wasn’t a zoo, the deal would be illegal. We enlisted an undercover agent who works with Amman, to investigate on the ground in Laos. Karl: Obviously to them it all just look like the tiger farms the same the same structure the same pattern of caging and so on. The agent filmed the lions shortly after their arrival. The lionesses had given birth. Karl: Some females were shipped in a pregnant stage which shouldn't have been happening, certainly not in the last trimester of pregnancy. After the trauma of travel, one lost all five cubs. The lioness with two surviving cubs was separated from her offspring. The investigator was told what their future would hold. Karl: They met some of the players but yeah they will get more lions, and they will breed these lions, they will sell live lions, cubs as pets and they will do the lion bone trade. The property looked nothing like a zoo: no outdoor signage, display cages or educational programmes. The only other animals were a lonely monkey … and some tigers. His experience told Amman it looked just like a captive breeding facility. But who signed the paperwork for such a deal? Who made it legal at a time when lion farms are facing closure? Transition to next act We took the CITES permits that an anonymous source leaked to us to the founder of Ban Animal Trading, Smaragda Louw. UPS SMARAGDA (GRAPHIC) Smaragda could see that the ten lions had been sold by a Free State lion farmer called Robbie Prinsloo of Farm Energie, and Edward Coetzer of African Pride Import and Export who shipped the Lions via Malaysia to Laos. Smaragda: The permit was in the name of Robbie Prinsloo. Edward Coetzer of African Pride was then the agent, he exported the animals to this so-called zoo in Laos. Smaragda had encountered Prinsloo’s Lions before in the course of her work. Smaragda: There's a lot of trade happening amongst all the people who breed lions. We know animals from the Rhino and Lion Park in Krugersdorp were sold to Farm Energy. It’s a reputational hazard for South Africa, fighting to restore its image as an ethical wildlife destination – YET a captive-bred lion that a tourist sees today… may end up in the hands of the tiger bone mafia tomorrow. We set out to find Farm Energie… Mac gets out car, goes to sign, checks out place… Prinsloo wouldn’t let us onto his farm, but said he loved his lions. Phone call: Mac: Robbie you’re speaking to MacFarlane from Carte Blanche. Prinsloo: Ja? Mac: I want to know about lions that went to Laos? Prinsloo: All the paperwork, as well as the legit paperwork from Laos government were for a zoo. I was actually proud to do this whole deal with them, because my lions will be going to a zoo, and millions of hundreds of people will be able to see them. Mac: All I can say is that you might have made a big big mistake, and sent your animals to the slaughter? Prinsloo: Ya, that’s… I don’t want to hear it, because I really love my lions. Through his lawyer, Prinsloo denied any involvement in the transaction. But he dropped names of two people involved in the deal, who are NOT on the CITES permits… Prinsloo: I can give you the woman who was helping me with all the paperwork, is Maryn. You know there were a guy from Joburg, that did this whole export thing, Gideon Fourie. Maryn is Maryn Goldblatt the former Head of the South African Predator Association which should be overseeing the big cat industry, including the animals’ welfare. It seems she didn’t know where the lions would end up either. Maryn: Yes, I just helped him with the permits, and everything with the agents, that’s all I did. Mac: The issue here, is where the animals are going to end up? Maryn: Any lion that we sell can end up either in a hunt, or killed or anything. They gave us their assurance that the animals are going to be in a good facility. So, I don’t know really what your problem is. Prinsloo told us that Gideon Fourie was the exporter, but he’s nowhere on the permits, and that might be with good reason: Ban Animal Trading encountered Fourie when he was convicted in 2017 of trafficking cockatoos, parrots, and monkeys and was given a suspended prison sentence and R85,000 fine. Smaragda intv: That export alone was worth R645,000, his companies kept exporting animals, and he continues as usual We tried to ask Fourie about this transaction… Call with Fourie: Fourie: Hello? Mac: Hi, it’s MacFarlane from Carte Blanche. BOOP BOOP BOOP (hangs up) In later texts, Fourie said he wanted nothing to do with our story. (graphic) Our final request for clarity… the exporter, Edward Coetzer of African Pride Import and Export who declined to speak, but sent documents showing it was the State Vet’s decision to allow lionesses to travel pregnant. Coetzer sent us these videos of the lions in Laos as proof of their “well-being”. UPS: VIDEO Barbara Creecy’s Department didn’t respond on why heavily pregnant lionesses were allowed to travel. CITES hasn't told us why the facility was given a zoo classification. Kieran: Laos announced that they would close their tiger farms, they have yet to do that. With no online presence, it proved impossible to speak to the Laos facility managers. In the meantime, South Africa’s lions continue to pay a high price. 11.05 END Promo 1 - 21 seconds A shipment of ten lions is sent from South Africa to an East Asian country well known for its illicit trade in wildlife body parts. UPSOUND: Karl: So you go into a restaurant and there's a big fish tank with a tiger skeleton in the fish tank. And then there's a little faucet on the side and you can filll your glass there and half and after dinner drink of tiger wine. We investigate what happened to these lions - and uncover that all is not as it seems. Promo two - 21 seconds It was a shipment of ten healthy lions from South Africa to an East Asian country, that caused animal activists to raise the alarm. Upsound : Kieran: we just hope that it isn't gonna turn into a lion farm on the other side. VO: Sent to a country well known for the illicit trade of animal parts - we investigate what really happened to these apex predators. Promo 3 - 21 seconds Lion farming… tiger bones and the illicit trade of wild animals and their body parts…. Upsound: Kieran: Laos announced that they would close their tiger farms, they have yet to do that. VO: We investigate how ten healthy lions shipped from South Africa, were allegedly condemned to die in East Asia

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Treatment/ Planning Lions in Lao This is a story about how lions are being used to supply bones to the tiger market in Asia for millions of rands. We have our heroes this side like Smaragda Louw from BAT who has been trying to make the South African law makers aware of this, and knows about the people who participate in this unethical market. Then there is Karl Amman, a film maker who has spent his life trying to expose harm that has come to animals like rhino horn trade, elephant tusk trade and tiger bone wine trade. They are the characters in this story that will speak to the audience on an emotional scale. Because this is about lions and tigers, I will ask my contacts at Lorypark zoo if I can film their lions and tigers, close up, really get intimate shots – we can do links as well there. Karl Amman is coming on the 26th – catching a connecting flight at OR Tambo back to Kenya from Europe. It wont be enough time for an interview, but he wants to sit down with me and help with footage etc. He has said he will sign the footage release for his footage from his doccie tiger bone wine trade – and he has sent that voice message about just covering the costs of the stringers on the ground who captured the footage in Laos. He explained it well in the message, and I think this clarifies everything and is something you’ll hopefully be happy with. In terms of capturing these animals – I need to go to 4PAWS who are in Bethlehem, they know the farm where these animals originated from, and will be able to speak about the history of this issue in South Africa: the issue in broadstrokes: We have captive bred lions around the country who just were bred and bred, and then Covid hit and none of them could be hunted. They were already exporting lion bones – to substitute for tiger bones… for the “Tiger bone/tiger wine” market – this was because people in Vietnam use it like Rhino horn- either grinding it into a powder or drinking the “wine” they make. So obviously there aren’t enough tigers in the world, so then “substituting” lions for the tiger bone trade – in which is the only real difference is SIZE. And so the end user in Asia often isn’t even getting the actual tiger bone wine, but lion bone. Our story will that even further… According to the permits: Farm Energie (Robbie Prinsloo) in Bethlehem has sold lionesses (2 of which were pregnant) the name on the permits is Mary Goldbaltt (who used to be Prinsloo) is now the CHIEF EXECUTIVE OF THE SOUTH AFRICAN PREDATORS ASSOCIATION – SAPA. Then we have African Pride Import & Exports (Edward Coetzer in Boksburg) on the permit which are the guys who get the permits and supposedly travel with the animals. Edward Coetzer’s business partner Philip Fourie has been given a criminal record for smuggling animals – but for some strange reason, South African laws allow someone to continue in the same trade after a conviction?! This is something Smargada can speak to the history of the import/exporters and their conduct. She will also speak to the fact that CITES and South African government are saying they want to close down the supply of lion bones to Asia, but they are doing it really slowly – like with this new legislation that adds in the “welfare” aspect of these animals. Then we get on the ground in Laos and that’s where we will have Karl and the footage there. Essentially he has had it transcribed and has given us the details of the place there – but these animals were sent to a “zoo” that isn’t even built yet. Also no one can afford zoos there, he will explain why Laos and how it works, and this is clearly and attempt to set up a breeding facility to then continue sending lions bones into the tiger bone trade because if South Africa is getting a little bit more difficult, those selling it know there will come a time when its ended. There are practically no animal welfare laws in Laos, and it’s a hub to country’s that surround it.
metadata.Summary: Filming schedule: DAY 1: 1. I would need a presenter to interview Smaragda – but we need time to actually be with her and her animals and see why she became this advocate for animals – she’s the type of crazy that goes and stands at zoo/circus corners holding banners and shouting at the owners to let the animals go. Her goal in life is the ban the trade in animals (BAT). AND I don’t think we’ve ever really highlighted this part of her, we have shown it in short snippets but we haven’t really told her story and who she is. She’s very passionate and I think quite a character that an audience can empathize with – you don’t have to be an animal lover to understand her. 2. I would then go to Boksburg and film outside African Pride, and we should go knock on their door to ask for an interview with a presenter. I think we need to see the faces of the people involved – so the audience can understand. 3. We would go to midrand and film the lions and tigers up close and personal – do some presenter links. DAY 2/3: 1. We need the presenter to come with us to Bethlehem and interview 4PAWS, we will then speak about the breeder of these lions and try to understand why they sold them/ their history etc – we will then call them and try to go to the farm – I’m not expecting to gain access there, but I do think we should be able to gain answers – they are one of many exporters of wild animals and I think we need to highlight the trade and the cruelty that comes with it. If we don’t get them, my plan is to still incorporate them with the presenter – we will do some snooping shots – showing the presenter researching them, trying to go see them, and this will add the dimension of secrecy that surrounds this trade – no one wants to be known as a lion exporter – its not something one fesses up to. I think we will need some time to also travel which take 3-4 hours – so travel time would be ideal. 2. We also still need to interview Karl Amman – and he said he will film himself and get footage of him from his doccies and things – so that is quite sorted – we can create his character as this person who wants to expose the trade and he has been able to have some impact in Asia with his documentary’s. It’s a very tough place to make a dent, so we can explain that. I’m not sure if we will have time enough with a presenter to do this, and I’m not sure Zoom can really help with the personal feel I have so I may just do the interview myself. Karl is german, his family are from kenya/Seychelles and he basically grew up in “wild” Africa and has been saddened and disheartened to see our animals used for pets/body parts etc So he can explain this as well really nicely – we can even include some of his childhood – giving him also a dimension in the piece.
metadata.Further information: We also need to put questions to CITES and the ministry – Barbara Creecy intv request. But I don’t expect either to agree, as they haven’t in the past. So with regards to their right of reply’s and the farm in Laos, I suggest we potentially have the presenter read them? Or Someone else voicing them? We need to come up with a different device for them, so the responses aren’t just washed away – but also aren’t boring.
